text:
maya (AE): Riverfront asked for a concise perf POC next week. Big ask: p95 < 300ms for single-turn at ~1k RPS. Can we sketch a minimal load plan + cost range?

sam (SalesEng): Do we know which model they'll run? lucas?

lucas (Riverfront): They prefer an open Llama variant. Start with 13B quantized. Budget is limited; they just need defensible numbers for infra conversations.

priya (ML Eng): 13B q4ish is a good starting point. For 1k RPS single-turn we'll rely on Redwood batching + KV caching. I propose two quick scenarios:
- Fast experiment: 4 GPUs (A10G-like), continuous batching, target effective concurrency ~64, short warmup.
- Conservative: 8 GPUs to hit headroom for kernel variance and network jitter.
Test window: 30s warmup, 8m steady-state, 2m cooldown.

chris (Infra): Recommend using Dedicated sandbox capacity for the run so noisy neighbors don't skew results. I'll create a 4-GPU reservation now; can expand if needed. No VPC required for the POC traffic.

sam (SalesEng): Priya please attach the k6 script you'll run and the exact metrics we'll report. Also we need a $/hour estimate for the SOW (placeholder OK).

priya (ML Eng): k6 example:
```bash
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m --summary-export=perf-summary.json post-gen.js
```
post-gen.js posts to /v1/generate with a single prompt. Payload snippet: 
```json
{"model":"llama-13b-q4o","input":"Extract key events from these logs"}
```
Metrics to include: p50/p95/p99 latencies, mean req/sec, tokens/sec, GPU util, batch size distribution, KV cache hit-rate, and error rate. We'll show tail latencies with and without batching.

maya (AE): Cost numbers for SOW? Lucas needs to sign off.

chris (Infra): For ballpark: A10G-equivalent on-demand ~ $2.5/hr each. 4 GPUs => $10/hr, 8 GPUs => $20/hr. Add Redwood Dedicated overlay + network (~$5-10/hr placeholder). For the engagement assume 4hr run window + 6-8h engineer time for prep/analysis.

priya (ML Eng): To clarify throughput math: single-turn 80 tokens @1k RPS => 80k tokens/sec. Raw per-GPU token rates vary a lot with batching/quantization. With our batching and q4 kernels we often see effective 4-10x improvements vs naive per-token baseline depending on request alignment. So instead of raw tokens/sec calc, we size by effective concurrency: aim for concurrency 48-128 across the pool. Practically, 4 GPUs may pass the test with optimized kernels and prompt lengths, otherwise fall back to 8 GPUs.

sam (SalesEng): OK include two options in the SOW: "baseline" (4 GPUs) and "buffered" (8 GPUs) with the $/hr ranges. Also include contingency for extra run time.

lucas (Riverfront): Fine. We'll approve up to the buffered option for a 4hr window. Please include a short runbook we can follow so we can observe metrics live.

priya (ML Eng): Runbook (short):
1) Prep: set MODEL=llama-13b-q4o, REDWOOD_KEY env, endpoint /v1/generate, 10 warmup requests.
2) Start harness: run k6 command above, monitor dashboard.
3) Watch panels: p95 latency, per-GPU util, batch size histogram, KV hit-rate, errors.
4) If p95 > 400ms for >2m, abort and scale to 8 GPUs or increase batch flush timeout.
5) Post-run: collect summary.json, server logs, and gpu stats (nvidia-smi logs).

chris (Infra): reserving now...

deploy-bot: reservation created sandbox-dedicated-13 (4 gpus) id rsv-9b7c.

chris (Infra): I've granted lucas view access to the sandbox dashboards.

maya (AE): Great. Priya, once you paste the final k6 script and small env snippet I'll copy into the SOW and schedule Thurs. :thumbsup:

priya (ML Eng): Posting minimal post-gen.js and env vars in next msg. Will include expected dashboard screenshots after a smoke run.

sam (SalesEng): Also adding a short note on security: POC uses public API keys; we'll rotate keys after POC. If they need a formal security questionnaire answered, I'll queue it with security.

lucas (Riverfront): Good. One last ask: include a short section on "what we measure" for their leadership: p95 latency, steady throughput, cost per 1M requests, and failure modes.

maya (AE): Will do. Thanks everyone.
